messages:
noah: Quick follow-up to the rollout metadata RFC — two recent PRs ended up with different shapes and we should pick a migration path before we ship. One PR (PR-A) uses a compact 'anchor_token' + hint bitset approach, the other (PR-B) uses explicit fields: origin, cohort, fallback_chain[], expiry_iso, and provenance_chain. Both work but have different upgrade stories.

leah: Can you paste short examples of each? makes tradeoffs easier to see.

noah: Sure — short sketches below. TL;DR: PR-A is space-efficient for storage/telemetry; PR-B is self-describing and easier for ops and audits.

noah: PR-A example:
```json
{"anchor_token":"ae4f...","hints":3,"flags": {"soft_gate": true}}
```

noah: PR-B example:
```json
{
  "origin":"model-registry/v2",
  "cohort":"canary-2026-03",
  "fallback_chain":["gpt-small-v1","gpt-small-v1-quant"],
  "expiry_iso":"2026-04-15T00:00:00Z",
  "provenance_chain":[{"commit":"abc123","deployed_by":"leah"}]
}
```

sam: My vote is for B for reads — ops and billing people will hate reversing a bitset. But A wins for high-vol tables where we attach metadata per inference.

ryan: We shouldn't do an either/or. Proposal: canonical canonicalization layer that emits both forms. Store canonical B in Control Plane for human/ops use, and emit compact A on tokenized telemetry and per-inference attach when size matters. Keep mapping deterministic and lossless where possible.

leah: How do we map provenance_chain to anchor_token without losing info? we can't fit arbitrary arrays into a token.

noah: Two options: 1) produce a deterministic content-hash anchor that references the full canonical record (like a pointer). We keep the full canonical record in the CP and use the hash as the compact reference. 2) embed a short provenance snapshot (last-commit + short cohort id) into the token for quick routing/fallback. Option 1 is smaller and more auditable; option 2 gives fast independent routing without a CP lookup.

sam: Ops latency concern: CP lookups in the hot-path are risky. If we require CP resolution for routing, Dedicated customers will push back. So any CP lookup must be best-effort with local cache fallback.

ryan: Agreed. Implementation sketch:
- CP stores canonical JSON (PR-B shape) keyed by anchor_hash.
- Runtime attaches anchor_hash to requests (PR-A token) and uses local LRU cache of canonical records; if miss, try CP with short timeout, else fall back to heuristics based only on token snapshot in request.

leah: For migration we should be additive and backward-compatible. Suggestion: Add two new top-level fields in rollout metadata: "anchor_hash" (string) and "anchor_snapshot" (optional object as a compact fallback). Consumers that understand full schema read anchor_hash -> fetch canonical. Older consumers ignore anchor_* fields and keep current behavior.

noah: +1. Also propose a validation rule: canonical records are immutable once anchored. If we need patching, issue a new anchor (new hash) and optional tombstone link to previous anchor. That preserves auditability.

sam: How about retention? We can't afford canonical records forever for every ephemeral canary. Maybe TTL of 90 days for ephemeral anchors and 2 years for GA anchors, with an index for audits.

ryan: That seems fine. We'll expose retention class in the canonical JSON as "lifecycle":"ephemeral|ga|archived". CP will enforce GC and provide an export for compliance before deletion.

leah: A few action items:
- write a short migration doc (noah) outlining fields and fallback semantics.
- runtime caching strategy doc (ryan).
- ops compatibility checklist (sam).
- add API to fetch canonical anchor by hash with 50ms p95 target (platform infra).

noah: I'll draft the migration doc and push an RFC appendix. For naming, let's avoid the word 'pin' in new fields — use 'anchor_hash' / 'anchor_snapshot' to reduce conceptual load.

ops-bot: Reminder: new datamodel changes require a schema migration plan and a rollback playbook. See /playbooks/schema-migration-template.

noah: Noted. I'll put a temporary feature-flag gate so we can roll the anchor propagation out in stages. Stage 1: emit anchor_hash on Control Plane events only. Stage 2: runtime emits compact anchor token for telemetry attach. Stage 3: runtime uses anchor_snapshot locally for routing when cache miss.

leah: Sounds good. If no objections by EOD I'll open the migration PR. :thumbsup:
